value:
During a Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at a sinister door. Enfield recalls Hyde trampling a girl, then paying her family £100 with a genuine cheque. Utterson studies Jekyll’s will, which leaves everything to Hyde if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon says Jekyll grew too fanciful and has never heard of Hyde. Keeping watch, Utterson accosts Hyde, who admits Jekyll is out, gives a Soho address, then snarls and disappears inside. Poole confirms Hyde has a key and all servants must obey him. Jekyll pales when Utterson mentions Hyde, refuses more, but says he can be rid of Hyde whenever he chooses. He asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when gone.

A maid saw Hyde cane Sir Danvers Carew to death. The mangled body bore a sealed envelope for Utterson, who identified Carew. Inspector Newcomen showed the broken stick, which Utterson recognized as Jekyll’s gift. They searched Hyde’s rooms, finding the other half and a burnt cheque book. Hyde had thousands at the bank, but few familiars, no photograph, and wildly differing descriptions.

Poole admits Utterson to Jekyll’s cabinet. Jekyll swears he will never see Hyde again. Jekyll gives Utterson a letter signed Edward Hyde, saying he burned the envelope, which had no postmark, and that Hyde dictated his will. Poole says no letter came except by post. Guest finds the murderer’s letter identical to Jekyll’s note. Utterson locks it in his safe, suspecting forgery.

After the murder, Hyde vanishes and rewards are offered. Jekyll resumes old friendships, then shuts his door; Poole says he is confined. Utterson finds Lanyon decayed, doomed, refusing Jekyll’s name. Lanyon dies within a fortnight. After the funeral, Utterson opens Lanyon’s sealed envelope, not to be opened till Jekyll’s death or disappearance. Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory, silent.

On another Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at the by-street door. Enfield says the Hyde affair is over, but Utterson admits he once saw Hyde and felt the same repulsion. Enfield reveals the door is Jekyll’s back way. Looking up, Utterson sees Jekyll sadly at the middle window. Jekyll says he is very low and it will not last long. He declines their walk, saying he dare not. When Utterson suggests talking from below, Jekyll’s smile becomes abject terror and the window is thrust down. The two men leave the court in silence, pale with horror, Utterson saying “God forgive us” twice.

Poole comes to Utterson at night, fearing foul play. They walk to Jekyll’s house, where servants huddle terrified. Poole leads Utterson to the cabinet; a changed voice refuses them. Poole claims Jekyll was murdered eight days ago and saw a masked dwarf—Mr. Hyde. Utterson resolves to break in. Poole strikes the door five times with an axe. Inside lies Hyde’s contorted body, a crushed phial nearby. They search for Jekyll but find only chemicals, a blasphemous book, a will naming Utterson, and a sealed packet. Utterson plans to read the documents and return before midnight.
